title: Two section-complex homotopies for a module replacement
statement: Let f:X→Y be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], F an X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], I an injective resolution of F and J an injective resolution of f_*F [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let K be a nonnegative complex of injective Y-modules, l:f_*I→K a quasi-isomorphism, and β:J→K satisfy J.ι⁰ β⁰=f_*(I.ι⁰)l⁰. Let a:Γ(X,I)≅Γ(Y,f_*I) have inverse in each degree equal to restriction along f⁻¹(Y)=X. Fix the standard abelian resolution R of the underlying sheaf of F and its explicit lift r:T_X I→R of the identity. Form the counit section map c:Γ(Y,J)→Γ(X,R) as described in [new-abelian-counit-resolution-calculation]. Then there exists a section-complex map q:Γ(Y,K)→Γ(X,R) which is a quasi-isomorphism, together with chain homotopies Γ(β)q∼c and (a.hom Γ(l))q∼Γ(r). This contains no equality of Ext maps and no degree p.

proof.text: Let R be the fixed abelian injective resolution of T_X F. Exact inverse image is left adjoint to abelian direct image, so f_*R has injective terms. Forget l to a quasi-isomorphism. To lift f_*r across it, extend by zero to integer complexes and factor this quasi-isomorphism through its mapping cylinder, whose inclusion is a degreewise mono quasi-isomorphism. Apply the bounded injective lifting property to the inclusion; precompose the result with the homotopy inverse to the cylinder projection. This gives k:T_Y K→f_*R with T(l)k homotopic to f_*r (013P part (1)). Restrict back to nonnegative complexes.

The augmentation equation for β, the lift equation for r, and the adjunction counit equation imply that T(β)k and counitResolutionAdjoint agree up to homotopy after the forgotten augmentation of J. That augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Uniqueness of maps into a bounded below injective complex gives a homotopy between the two maps. Apply abelian sections and the restriction identification to obtain the first asserted homotopy. Apply sections to the lifting homotopy, and use the degreewise equation for a.inv, to obtain the second. Set q=Γ(k) followed by the restriction identification.

Sections of r is a quasi-isomorphism because both complexes have section-acyclic terms, by forgotten injective acyclicity and the acyclic comparison theorem. Sections of l is a quasi-isomorphism by the module pushforward injectives sections theorem (extend by zero and reflect quasi-isomorphisms to obtain its nonnegative-indexed form). The second homotopy and two-out-of-three imply that q is a quasi-isomorphism. No acyclicity of f_*F and no exactness of module pullback are assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem abelian_replacement_section_homotopies {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {F : X.Modules} (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J : InjectiveResolution ((pushforward f).obj F)) (K : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℕ)
    (hK : ∀ n : ℕ, Injective (K.X n))
    (l : ((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex ⟶ K)
    (hl : QuasiIso l) (β : J.cocomplex ⟶ K)
    (hβ : J.ι.f 0 ≫ β.f 0 = (pushforward f).map (I.ι.f 0) ≫ l.f 0)
    (a : ((moduleSections X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex ≅
      ((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj
        (((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex))
    (ha : ∀ n : ℕ, a.inv.f n = (presheaf (I.cocomplex.X n)).map
      (eqToHom (by simp) : (⊤ : X.Opens) ⟶ f ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : Y.Opens)).op) :
    ∃ q : ((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj K ⟶
        ((abelianSections X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj
          (standardAbelianResolution X F).cocomplex,
      QuasiIso q ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy
        (((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).map β ≫ q)
        (counitSectionMap f F J)) ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy
        ((a.hom ≫ ((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).map l) ≫ q)
        (((abelianSections X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).map
          (forgottenResolutionMap X I)))
